title: The telephone
description: Name the parts of a phone, and talk about a call.
grammar: gender and articles, and the words for a call
grammarNote: The names of the things on a phone are nouns, and each one has its own gender.

explanation.summary: Everyone carries one of these, so the words are worth knowing. The names are a mixture of masculine and feminine, and the call itself is a noun you can make.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: El teléfono, el móvil, el botón, el altavoz y el cargador are masculine. La llamada, la pantalla, la red y la batería are feminine. El botón is the button you press, and la pantalla is the screen you look at.

sections.heading: Talking about a call
sections.body: Hacer una llamada is to make a call, and la llamada is the call itself. The words for the state of the phone are ordinary sentences: la batería está baja, the battery is low, el teléfono está en la mesa, the phone is on the table.

examples.es: el teléfono está en la mesa
examples.en: the phone is on the table

examples.es: hago una llamada a mi madre
examples.en: I make a call to my mother

items.note: Masculine: el tono. It is also el tono de llamada, the ringtone.
Masculine: el botón. The accent marks the stress.
Feminine: la batería. The accent marks the stress.

drills.meaning: the phone is on the table
I make a call to my mother
drills.note: Llamada is feminine, so una llamada.
